annotation.title_clean: 智慧機器人之產品責任問題研析
annotation.title_en: Analysis of Product Liability Issues for Intelligent Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: 立法院 (Legislative Yuan, Taiwan) – 議題研析, 撰稿人：李淑瓊
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Taiwan Legislative Yuan issue brief on product liability for intelligent robots. It reviews the Civil Code art. 191-1 and Consumer Protection Act arts. 7-9, robot legal status debates, and the EU AI Liability Directive's proposed withdrawal. It concludes existing law is inadequate and recommends studying amendments or a special statute.
key_provisions_or_claims: Civil Code art. 191-1 and Consumer Protection Act arts. 7-9 struggle with autonomous learning robots' causation and complex supply chains.
Opacity of robot decision-making creates evidentiary burdens for victims.
Granting AI personhood or a new legal category is debated; it may weaken human designers' liability.
EU AI Liability Directive proposal (2022) was slated for withdrawal in the Commission's 2025 work programme.
Recommends balancing consumers and supply-chain actors and evaluating amendments or a special law for Taiwan.
